🇺🇸 US tech outages expose fragile infrastructure — and a fumbling official response
The Trump administration is under fire from both allies and opponents over its handling of a string of major [technology disruptions](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/77902) across the country, the WSJ reported.
Officials claim there is no evidence of a coordinated cyberattack. Secretary of State Mark Rubio said there is “zero evidence” that any of these incidents were related. Yet this has done little to prevent a surge of speculation online over the faltering response from top officials, notes the publication.
🔴 Microsoft’s global outage disrupted email and other services
🔴 [ An FAA ground stop](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/77746) led to nearly 20,000 flight cancellations, with officials pointing to problems involving outdated air-traffic control technology 
🔴 [JPMorgan Chase](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/77876) reported a software bug disrupting transactions
🔴 NSA’s classified internal communications network reportedly went offline amid a software update
Democratic lawmakers and prominent conservatives have slammed the administration’s handling of the incidents.
➡️ Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy and DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin initially blamed outdated US air-traffic control technology but failed to identify the precise cause
➡️ Mullin said there was no evidence of a cyberattack, while acknowledging that nothing could be ruled out
➡️ Brian Harrell, who served as DHS infrastructure protection chief under Trump, said the officials’ muddled explanations and media strategy were eroding public confidence.
The outages laid bare the country’s excessive reliance on aging systems, the report noted, and how easily technical failures can be read as something sinister when official communication lags.

events.text:
🇺🇸 US Patriot missile crisis exposes decades of industrial decay
The Pentagon is struggling to ramp up Patriot interceptor production as stockpiles shrink, with a critical component exposing deep vulnerabilities in America’s munitions industry, reports WSJ.
The US had burned through roughly 35% of its already [strained missile inventory ](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/76997)by the end of July amid the war on Iran (CSIS).
Yet decades of consolidation and offshoring have left US weapons production vulnerable, notes the report.
🔴 advanced PAC-3 MSE interceptors rely on carbonized rayon, a heat-resistant material used to line rocket nozzles
🔴 the only supplier whose product is qualified for the missiles is France's ArianeGroup - its fabric is processed by US company Park Aerospace before reaching L3Harris and ultimately Lockheed Martin
🔴 extreme qualification standards make rapid substitution nearly impossible; any alternative can take years of testing and still fail at the final stage
🔴 post-Cold War cuts reduced major contractors from 51 to just five, and eliminated most domestic aerospace-grade rayon production
🔴 heavy overlap among second- and third-tier suppliers across Patriot, THAAD and other systems means disruption at one node risks multiple programs
🔴 French authorities and industry favor domestic military needs, limiting extra allocations for the US
PAC-3 MSE missiles cost around $4 million, take approximately two years to manufacture and contain hundreds of components.
The Pentagon has signed multiyear agreements to boost PAC-3 MSE output to around 2,000 annually by the end of 2030, and is pursuing alternative rayon sources.
But new materials must undergo lengthy qualification tests - while ArianeGroup plans to expand French production only by 2028, and potentially establish a US facility around 2030.

events.text:
🤥 Trump has weaponized the Treasury – but at what cost to the US dollar?
US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent is at the forefront of President Donald Trump's economic war against Canada, Cuba and Iran – a campaign that, as Responsible Statecraft argues, can be no less ruthless than a shooting war.
🔶 After Trump suggested that Canada could become the US' 51st state, he dispatched Bessent to wield “economic force” to “get rid of that artificially drawn line” between the two countries. Bessent also sought to pit Alberta against Ottawa and even backed Alberta's independence referendum, which was ultimately defeated
🔶 Rather than send US troops into Cuba, Trump put Bessent in charge of the island's economic strangulation. The campaign has failed to bring about regime change but has inflicted considerable hardship on ordinary Cubans, leaving many without electricity, water, food and medicine. The UN has highlighted Washington's actions as being “incompatible with basic principles of international human rights law,” leading to deaths among Cuban civilians and children
🔶 Iran has become another target. Secretary of State Marco Rubio recently boasted that “the economic pain that is being inflicted on Iran right now is extraordinary.” He argued that Washington did not need to launch broader military strikes against Iran because it was “achieving the same objective through economic means and economic pressure.” Yet despite reports that Iran's economy could contract by 25%, the Islamic Republic has shown considerable resilience and continues to maintain control over the Strait of Hormuz.
Responsible Statecraft argues that the Trump administration has turned the dollar and economic sanctions into far more powerful weapons than previous US administrations. But economic experts warn that the more Washington weaponizes its economic leverage, the more countries around the world will look to move away from the US dollar.
